extracted.intended_audience: general public and policymakers interested in tech policy and congressional oversight
extracted.subtask_description: A news report summarizing testimony by a tech CEO before Congress, highlighting lawmakers' questions and the company's responses on data privacy, content moderation, ads transparency, and regulatory issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of responsibility / apology
rubrics_metrics.description: "We didn't take a broad enough view of our responsibility, and that was a big mistake. It was my mistake, and I'm sorry," the co-founder and CEO said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures whether the company leadership publicly acknowledges failures and apologizes; the article frames this as a notable shift in Facebook's stance and as part of a 'broader philosophical shift' toward taking greater responsibility for user content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing users about how their data is used
rubrics_metrics.description: The company began informing users who were affected; senators asked why Facebook didn't inform users back in 2015 when it first discovered that user data had been sold to Cambridge Analytica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates timeliness, reach and clarity of user notifications (e.g., providing a help-page check); anti-patterns include delayed or partial notifications and relying on confusing long policies instead of clear notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and readability of privacy policies
rubrics_metrics.description: "Long privacy policies are very confusing," Zuckerberg said. "If you make it long and spell out all the detail, then you're probably going to reduce the percent of people who read it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether policies are understandable to typical users and whether simplified explanations are provided; considers user expectations for different services and the need for clearer, shorter disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of notifying regulators (FTC) and compliance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook did not inform the FTC of the improper data sharing, Zuckerberg says.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the company timely reports breaches or improper sharing to regulators and follows legal obligations; includes whether the company considered matters 'closed' without adequate follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with FTC consent decree
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the terms of that decree, Facebook is required to 'obtain users' affirmative consent' before sharing their data. Zuckerberg denied that the data-sharing violated Facebook's 2011 consent decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks legal interpretation and adherence to existing consent decrees; examines whether platform architecture (e.g., Facebook Platform) effectively circumvented affirmative consent requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing misuse by third-party developers
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook has blamed Aleksandr Kogan ... for violating Facebook's terms of service. Blumenthal showed an agreement claiming broad rights; Zuckerberg said he had not seen that text and that the app review team would have been responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates vetting, review, and oversight processes for developers and apps (app review team responsibilities), including contractual protections and follow-up when developers violate terms; anti-patterns: inadequate review, lack of enforcement, no accountability for review teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of data recipients and completeness of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Zuckerberg also said that Kogan sold data to other companies ... he said he would provide lawmakers with more detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the company fully discloses which third parties received user data and provides complete, timely information to lawmakers and the public; partial answers or promises to follow up are weaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and completeness of testimony / willingness to follow up
rubrics_metrics.description: Zuckerberg said he didn't know the answer to several questions or that he would have to check with his team ... he said he would provide lawmakers with more detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures whether the CEO provides complete, accurate answers in testimony and promptly supplies follow-up details; incomplete answers or deferrals reduce credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content moderation effectiveness (hate speech and harmful language)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Determining if something is hate speech is very linguistically nuanced," he said, and the error rate is high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how well the platform identifies and removes hate speech and harmful language, balancing nuance and false positives; considers human review, policy definitions of hate speech, and risks of over-/under-enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limitations of AI in moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: Zuckerberg noted that Facebook has had success using artificial intelligence tools to police and enforce communication by blocking terrorist propaganda, but he says it's more difficult to identify hate speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses AI tools' current capabilities, error rates, areas of success (e.g., terrorist content) and limits (nuanced hate speech), and the need for improved models and human oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election security and defense against foreign interference
rubrics_metrics.description: "There are people in Russia whose job it is to try to exploit our systems ... This is an arms race," he said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates investments, technical safeguards, monitoring, disinformation detection, and collaboration with authorities to protect elections; treats foreign actors as persistent threats requiring ongoing investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and verification for political and issue ads
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook recently began requiring location verification for groups purchasing political or issue ads ... senators asked whether shell corporations could be used to get around that system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses ad transparency measures (who paid, where they are based), effectiveness of verification processes, and vulnerability to evasion (e.g., shell corporations); looks for provenance tracking and disclosure mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform neutrality and Section 230 implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Sen. Ted Cruz ... 'The predicate for Section 230 immunity is that you are a neutral public forum,' he said. 'Do you consider yourself a neutral public forum or are you engaged in political speech?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the platform's content policies and enforcement practices affect its claim to immunity under Section 230, including whether platform actions constitute editorial/political speech versus neutral hosting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of flagging violations — proactive detection vs user reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sen. Chris Coons ... asked why Facebook puts the burden on users to flag content that needs to be taken down. Zuckerberg cited the 'sheer volume' of material on Facebook and said new hires and AI tools will help improve the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures how proactive the platform is in detecting violations versus relying on user reports; considers resource allocation (staff, AI), response times, and scalability for high-volume platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing discriminatory ad targeting (housing and rental discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We can't wait five years for Facebook to get rid of housing discrimination content," Coons said, referring to allegations that the site lets housing and rental companies restrict who can see their ads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses policies, detection, and enforcement specifically aimed at discriminatory ad practices; includes urgency and effectiveness of remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: User understanding of cross-site tracking and device activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Sen. Cory Gardner ... brought up the example of a user browsing a news site that has a 'Facebook button on it' ... 'Do you think users understand that?' Gardner asked. 'I think the answer is probably yes,' Zuckerberg said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks whether users are aware of tracking mechanisms (plugins, buttons, cross-device tracking) and whether the company provides clear explanations and controls for such tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with law enforcement and special counsel investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: "I want to be careful here because that, our work with the special counsel is confidential ... I am not aware of a subpoena, I believe there may be [a subpoena], but I know we are working with them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the company's level of cooperation, disclosure where permissible, and balancing confidentiality with congressional oversight; looks at provision of documents and responsiveness to lawful requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate accountability and internal personnel actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Zuckerberg said that Facebook's app review team would have been responsible for that agreement and that nobody from that team has been fired over this scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates internal accountability mechanisms, whether responsible personnel are disciplined or restructured after failures, and whether systemic changes are implemented rather than only surface-level responses.
